functional_compartments.name: Superficial head
functional_compartments.function_note: Documented separately-innervated head -- median nerve, matching its embryological/functional grouping with the other thenar muscles.
functional_compartments.source: Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

relative_muscle_spindle_abundance.notes: Comparable across muscles of different size because it is normalised by predicted count rather than by mass.

functional_compartments.name: Deep head
functional_compartments.function_note: Deep head is classically described as ulnar-nerve innervated (superficial head median-nerve) -- the hand's parallel to adductor magnus's dual innervation in the thigh -- though cadaveric studies find this split considerably more variable in practice than the textbook model: the superficial head carries dual median+ulnar innervation in roughly 30% of specimens, and the deep head's innervation pattern (including occasional median-only supply) also varies (adjusted for this nuance after adversarial fact-check, see docs/VERIFICATION.md).
functional_compartments.source: Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transverse on the palm over the thenar eminence, medial to abductor pollicis brevis and superficial to the first metacarpal cortex.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Thenar group; superficial and deep heads are separately resolvable, divided by an intramuscular fascia.
structures_at_risk: flexor pollicis longus tendon (a landmark, not a hazard)
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: A primary driver of the thumb-in-hand pattern in cerebral palsy, where it interferes with hygiene, risks skin breakdown and blocks grasp, pinch and release.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part I -- Distal Upper Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(3):107 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17030107

relative_muscle_spindle_abundance.method: actual spindle count divided by the count predicted from muscle mass, by Banks' allometric correction
relative_muscle_spindle_abundance.notes: Extramuscular nerve trunk length 1.70 +/- 0.12 cm. Comparable across muscles of different size because it is normalised by predicted count rather than by mass.
relative_muscle_spindle_abundance.source: Xie P, Jiang Y, Zhang X, Yang S, 'The Study of Intramuscular Nerve Distribution Patterns and Relative Spindle Abundance of the Thenar and Hypothenar Muscles in Human Hand', PLoS One 7(12):e51538 (2012), doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0051538 -- 40 hands from 20 adult cadavers, modified Sihler's stain with haematoxylin-eosin spindle counts

notes: A genuinely compartmented muscle, and this atlas's split into superficial and deep heads is confirmed by it: the superficial head is supplied by the recurrent branch of the MEDIAN nerve and the deep head by the deep branch of the ULNAR nerve, and each head has its own fibre direction, origin and insertion. The two are separable as independent flaps. For injection this means the two heads must be treated as two targets on two different nerves, not as one muscle.

trigger_points.location_description: Palpated against the metacarpal shaft with the thumb MCP slightly flexed, over the flexor pollicis brevis belly ulnar to abductor pollicis brevis.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: No distinct published Travell & Simons figure for flexor pollicis brevis; clinically its trigger points give local palmar thumb/MCP-sesamoid pain and pinch fatigue, merging with the thenar adductor-opponens referral pattern (Ch. 39).
trigger_points.notes: Distinguish from sesamoiditis (point bony tenderness) and trigger thumb (A1 nodule, triggering).
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 1 -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded hand intrinsic muscle reference document (Ch. 39 thenar adductor-opponens pattern, applied by clinical analogy; no separate flexor pollicis brevis figure is published)

clinical.compiled_by: repository owner (physician); hand_intrinsic_muscles_reference_v1.html, compiled 03/09/2026. Source hierarchy used. (1) Peer-reviewed anatomical and biomechanical studies (bibliographic data and abstracts retrieved via PubMed/NCBI, 01–03/09/2026; DOIs linked in the reference list); (2) reference textbooks — Standring (Gray's Anatomy, 42nd ed., 2021), Kapandji (2007), Green's Operative Hand Surgery (8th ed., 2022), Brand & Hollister (1999); (3) Simons, Travell & Simons, The Trigger Point Manual Vol. 1, 2nd ed. (1999) and 3rd ed. (2019) for trigger-point (TrP) referral patterns; (4) StatPearls/NCBI Bookshelf for cross-checking. No item below relies on blogs or unattributed aggregators; where secondary TrP summaries were used to confirm Travell & Simons figures, they are graded accordingly in the verification table.
clinical.function_biomechanics: Flexes the thumb MCP and flexes/medially rotates the 1st metacarpal — the "flexion" limb of opposition; a key MCP stabiliser during pinch, working as a force couple with AdP against the extensor apparatus. Loss of the ulnar (deep) head contributes to Jeanne's MCP hyperextension in pinch [1][20][26][31]. EMG shows thenar recruitment (APB→FPB→OP) grading with opposition force and object size [20].
clinical.adjacent_structures: Relations · closed sacs: Ulnar to OP, medial part deep to APB; the radial bursa and the thumb MCP capsule/volar plate–sesamoid apparatus are its closed-space partners — sesamoid arthrosis or sheath tenosynovitis (trigger thumb at the A1 pulley) present in exactly its territory [1][34].

trigger_points.referred_pain: No distinct published Travell & Simons figure; clinically FPB TrPs give local palmar thumb/MCP-sesamoid pain and pinch fatigue, merging with the adductor–opponens pattern [24].
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: sustained pinch, jar-opening, texting. Palpate against the metacarpal with the MCP slightly flexed; distinguish from sesamoiditis (point bony tenderness) and trigger thumb (A1 nodule, triggering).
trigger_points.source: [24] Simons DG, Travell JG, Simons LS. Travell & Simons' Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 1: Upper Half of Body. 2nd ed. Baltimore: Williams & Wilkins; 1999 — Ch. 39 (adductor & opponens pollicis), Ch. 40 (interossei, lumbricals, abductor digiti minimi; pp. 786-793).

pain_referred_into_this_muscle_from: FPL (deep palmar thumb, distal), opponens pollicis, pronator teres (volar radial wrist into thumb), palmaris longus (superficial palm) [24]; median nerve, C6, MCP/sesamoid arthrosis, UCL injury [35].
clinical.caveat: Most myofascial hand pain is imported: shoulder-girdle, arm and forearm TrPs project distally far more often than intrinsic TrPs project proximally. Patterns below are the prototype maps of Simons, Travell & Simons (Vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1999; 3rd ed., 2019) — screening guides, not fingerprints; individual spread is wide [24][25]. Non-myofascial mimics are listed per zone for the same working position [5][29][31][35]. TrP → = habitual referred-pain direction of that muscle's trigger points (Simons, Travell & Simons 1999/2019); patterns are prototypes — individual variation is wide.
